was an industrial-scale 18th-century phenomenon.

Silver built the 16th century. Gold defined the 18th century.
86,000,000 kg +
Silver, driving the Spanish imperial state
from the mountains of Mexico and Peru.
1,700,000 kg
Gold, driving the 18th-century frontier
economies of Brazil and New Granada.
The meticulous records of the Spanish Cartas Cuentas and Portuguese mints correct centuries of
myth. While silver was the abundant metal of empire, gold-though physically scarce and prone to
illicit trade-commanded 25% of the hemisphere's purchasing power, forever altering the global
economy not during the era of conquest, but on the eve of independence.
